The second reference photo is the character: keep the exact same face sculpt and head proportions. Change only what this description says: Photograph of a hand-sculpted stop-motion claymation figure, matte plasticine with fingerprints, tool marks and pressed texture, soft studio lighting, highly detailed, in exactly the style of the reference photos. A grotesque disfigured old man with an oversized bobble head, mottled skin with age spots, small sunken bloodshot eyes in swollen red-rimmed lids, a large ear with a fat hanging lobe, thick neck, hunched broad shoulders, head turned three-quarters toward the viewer's right. Head type: a huge tall lumpy dome skull with dents and bumps, like the master reference, sallow yellowish clay skin, bald crown with stringy grey clay hair tufts above the ears, raised grey clay wrinkle ridges on the forehead. A crude, poorly made homemade gas mask of patched and badly stitched brown leather over his nose and mouth, crooked mismatched buckled straps, a dented tin can stuffed with rags as a makeshift filter, eyes visible above. Wearing stained grey mechanic coveralls, a worn leather tool belt with rusty tools and pouches, his right fist grips a crude spear: a long wooden pole with a rusty jagged blade lashed to the top with wire and rag, held upright with the blade above his shoulder; his LEFT fist tightly grips a rusty woodcutter axe by its long wooden handle, the axe resting up on his left shoulder with the blade behind his shoulder, carried in his hand, not strapped to his back, a dented rusty green oxygen tank strapped upright on his back with frayed canvas straps over both shoulders, its brass valve poking up behind his shoulder and a ribbed black rubber hose running from the valve over his shoulder into the side of his gas mask. A rusty orange pressed-clay backdrop. FACING: exactly like the first reference photo, his body is in three-quarter view and his head and face are turned about 45 degrees toward the RIGHT side of the image (the viewer's right), nose pointing right; never turned to the left side and never straight on. Three-quarter view from the hips up, whole head, mask and weapons inside the frame with a little space above the head, figure centred, square 1:1 composition. SCALE (the same for every figure in the series): the figure is the same size in the frame as in the first reference photo, the bobble head the same size relative to the body, and weapons true to scale with the hands, never oversized or tiny. Both hands are full and both are tight clenched fists, knuckles toward the camera: the right fist grips the held weapon, the left fist grips the second weapon by its handle as described. Avoid: text, logo, letters, watermark, brand marks, sports team logo, red chevrons or triangles on the mask, full-face goalie mask covering the forehead and eyes, white screaming ghost mask, black hooded robe, pins in a grid, extra fingers, deformed hands, cropped head, photo of a real person, cartoon outline, flat 2D, face turned to the left, mirrored pose, long finger blades, clawed glove with four long knives, red and green striped sweater, brown fedora
